minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission revoted three prior actions by roll call to cure an open meeting law violation, and approved the counsel's response.
minutes.summary: Held by Zoom only with two of three commissioners present. After public comment from John Bowen, Town Counsel explained that voice votes at the November 21 meeting, with a remote member, breached the open meeting law. The commission approved his response letter and redid the earlier votes by roll call, then adjourned over Mr. Bowen's objection that other agenda items had not been taken up.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted 2-0 by roll call to approve Town Counsel's response to an open meeting law complaint and to send it to the complainant and the Division of Open Government.
Town Counsel said voice votes at the November 21 meeting, which included a remote member, breached the open meeting law.
The commission redid by roll call, 2-0, the vote on the response to the eminent domain taking from the interim town manager.
The commission also revoted by roll call, 2-0, the two Rainmaker license votes, for professional service and maintenance support.
The chair, on advice of counsel, passed over the remaining agenda items, including cemetery capital funding projects, and the meeting adjourned.

why_it_matters: Earlier commission votes, including those on the Rainmaker records-system licenses, were cured by roll call, so they now stand on a cleaner record, while cemetery capital funding and DPW updates have not been taken up.

A resident said he will file a warrant article on how sale-of-lots funds may be used; this was an allegation from the public and the board did not discuss it, but it could become a vote at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Town Counsel's response letter, to be finalized and sent to the complainant, the town manager and the Division of Open Government.
A future meeting date for the deferred items: DPW director updates, cemetery capital funding projects and the meeting schedule.
